newsitem.title: USA: Crouse Hospital, N.Y., says to sell taxable debt.
newsitem.headline: Crouse Hospital, N.Y., says to sell taxable debt.

text.p: In what underwriters are calling the first offering of its kind, Crouse Health Hospital in Syracuse, N.Y., plans to issue $35 million of taxable, variable-rate demand notes.

The underwriter, Ziegler Securities, said similar deals in the past have obtained financing through state agencies, which required longer waiting periods and usually only provided fixed-rate financing at tax-exempt rates.

On the Crouse deal, which will be backed by a letter of credit from LaSalle National Bank in Chicago, the bonds will carry an initial interest rate of 5-1/2 percent. The rate will then vary weekly, reset by Ziegler.

"So many not-for-profits have the need to act quickly to fund acquisitions and other capital needs," said James Normile, a partner at the law firm of Whitman Breed Abbott & Morgan, which helped structure the refinancing. "This type of deal will not be a substitute for traditional tax-exempt bonds in every instance, but for a number of borrowers it represents a fast and efficient solution to capital needs."

James O'Keefe, the senior banker on the deal for Ziegler, said variable-rate demand notes have historically traded in the range of five percent to 6.50 percent. O'Keefe said that range compares favorably with a New York State fixed-rate tax-exempt issue, even after adding the fees for the letter of credit and annual remarketing.

"Because the debt is taxable, the funds can be utilized to accomplish a number of very necessary growth activities, such as physician or insurer-related joint ventures -- projects for which tax-exempt funds cannot be utilized," O'Keefe said.
